evidence.excerpt: End-to-end encryption prevents direct inspection of protocol message content, but metadata features — packet sizes, inter-arrival times, and flow directions — remain observable. We investigate whether finite automaton models of IoT device communication behaviour can be inferred from such metadata alone. Twenty-two consumer IoT device types were placed in a controlled network testbed; traffic was captured over 72-hour periods under scripted usage scenarios. Message sequences were reconstructed from metadata clusters using a k-means procedure with k determined by a silhouette criterion. RPNI was applied to the resulting labelled sequences. The inferred automata reproduce 79–93% of transitions present in models derived from unencrypted reference captures of the same devices. Devices with highly regular behaviour (smart plugs, sensors) yielded better models than devices with irregular patterns (smart cameras during video streaming). The approach is evaluated on its suitability for network anomaly detection in encrypted environments.
